prompt:
A sharp close-up photograph, camera level with the base, of a neon acrylic ring-stacking puzzle on a black photographic table: a flat base with THREE upright pegs standing on it, marked A (left), B (middle) and C (right).

It carries 6 round disks of clearly different widths -- disk 1 (the narrowest) is magenta, disk 2 is yellow, disk 3 is cyan, disk 4 is lime, disk 5 is violet, disk 6 is orange (the widest) -- and every disk has its own size number printed large on its face. The stacking rule is the usual one -- a disk rests either on the base or on a disk wider than itself, never on a narrower one.

At the start all 6 disks are stacked on peg A, widest at the bottom. Someone now moves the whole tower onto peg C in the FEWEST possible moves -- that shortest solution takes exactly 63 moves -- lifting one disk at a time, always the top disk of a peg, and never putting a wider disk onto a narrower one.

Show the toy EXACTLY as it stands immediately after move 43 of that shortest solution: not the starting tower, not the finished tower, not any other moment. Every disk must sit on the peg it really occupies at that instant, in the correct order, and a peg that holds no disk must be drawn empty.

Keep the picture clean: no move list, no annotations, no captions. The only characters in the image are the letters on the base and the number printed on each disk.
easy_question: Never mind how well it is drawn. Does this picture show an acrylic ring-stacking puzzle: a base with three upright pegs carrying round stacking disks of graduated widths? A realistic photo, an illustration, a schematic or a clean diagram ALL count as yes. Answer NO only if the image instead shows just a blank card or plain panel that prints an answer with none of that shown, or shows something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

reference.q_notext: The peg letters on the base and the size number printed on each disk do not count. Apart from those, is there a separate line of text or numbers that lists moves or states where the disks sit? Answer yes or no.
